outcome: Every device connecting to the clinical network is identified, profiled and placed in the right segment automatically.
overview: Hospital networks carry a large population of devices that nobody in IT provisioned — infusion pumps, imaging modalities, contractor laptops, personal phones on clinical wireless — many of which cannot take an agent, and several that must not be touched at all. FortiNAC profiles what is connected, decides what each device may reach, and enforces that decision at the switch port or wireless controller — and the first deliverable is usually the surprise, a device inventory nobody had. Enforcement follows only after clinical engineering has confirmed that nothing safety-relevant is about to be disconnected.

benefits.text: Every connected device is profiled and attributed, including the ones IT never provisioned
benefits.limits: Profiling identifies device type with high but not perfect confidence; a mis-profiled clinical device placed in the wrong segment is a patient-safety event, not a ticket

benefits.text: Unmanaged devices are placed in a bounded segment rather than on the general network
benefits.limits: Enforcement depends on the switching and wireless estate supporting dynamic assignment; older access equipment may need replacing first

benefits.text: A device that appears on the network out of policy can be found and attributed quickly
benefits.limits: Location accuracy depends on switch port mapping being maintained; a patch panel change nobody recorded degrades it silently

residency: Runs on-premises inside the hospital estate; device and session data stay within the operator’s network and no clinical data is inspected

notFor.situation: An estate already running another network access control platform in enforcement
notFor.why: Two admission controllers on the same ports is an outage waiting for a coincidence

notFor.situation: An access layer that cannot do dynamic VLAN or policy assignment
notFor.why: Without enforcement at the port the platform is a very good inventory and nothing more

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Fortinet implementation partner, working alongside hospital clinical engineering · Duration: 10–16 weeks to enforcement on corporate classes; clinical classes on clinical engineering’s schedule
Support model: Vendor support for the platform; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed operations with an agreed profiling-review cycle.
1) Deploy and observe — platform in monitor mode, profiling across the estate, no enforcement
2) Inventory and attribute — device classes named and claimed by clinical engineering and IT
3) Design — segment model, holding-segment behaviour and the class-by-class enforcement order
4) Enforce and hand over — enforcement enabled per class with sign-off, operations handed over
deliverables: An unknown device connecting to any access port lands in the holding segment, verified by test
Every enforced device class has a recorded clinical or IT owner sign-off
A device can be located to a switch port and physical area from the admission log
